Rashi on Shabbat 27a:10:1.hebrew: ה"ג דרב פפא אמר אף כל לאתויי כלאים - אף כל דתנא דרישא, דקאמר אף כל בגדים סתם צמר ופשתים, לאו לפרושי בגדים סתומים דטומאה קא אתי — דבשאר טומאה ודאי מטמאו שאר בגדים, דאיתרבו מאו בגד — אלא לפרושי בגד האמור בכלאים סתם, ובגד כלאים שעטנז וגו'. הלכך, לרב פפא לא מפיק האי תנא מילתיה דהאי תנא, והך פירוקא דסיפא איהו אמרה; ולא איתמר כדאמרת ליה אליבא דרבא, דמפליג בין ג' על ג' לשלשה על שלשה, אלא הכי איתמר: רב פפא אמר, לא מפיק האי תנא מאידך תנא, דאף כל לאתויי כלאים. דכי הוה מוקמינן ליה כרבא, הוה צריך לפלוגי: דכיון דאף כל לטומאת שרצים נמי אתא, על כרחיך אף כל למעוטינהו משלש על שלש כדין נגעים, ואו בגד לרבויי שלשה על שלשה. ואף על גב דלא מטמו שאר בגדים בנגעים — דהא נתמעטו בתרי מיעוטי — איתרבו בשרצים. אבל לרב פפא, לא מיבעי לן לפלוגי: דכיון דאתרבו שאר בגדים לשרצים, איתרבו לכל תורת צמר ופשתים — בין לשלש, בין לשלשה:
Rashi on Shabbat 27a:10:1.english: This is the correct reading: “For Rav Pappa said: ‘Even all’ is to include diverse kinds” - The [phrase] “even all” of the first Tanna — who said: “Even all [mentions of] garments without qualification [in the Torah are] wool and linen” — did not come to explain unspecified garments of ritual impurity, for regarding other ritual impurity, other garments certainly become ritually impure, as they were included from [the verse] “or a garment” (Leviticus 11:32); rather, [it came] to explain the garment mentioned in [the prohibition of] diverse kinds without qualification: “and a garment of diverse kinds, sha’atnez...” (Leviticus 19:19). Therefore, according to Rav Pappa, this Tanna does not diverge from the words of that Tanna, and this resolution at the end [of the discussion], he [Rav Pappa] stated it; and it was not stated as you stated it according to Rava, who distinguishes between three by three [fingerbreadths] and three by three [handbreadths], but rather this is how it was stated: “Rav Pappa said: This Tanna does not diverge from the other Tanna, for ‘even all’ is to include diverse kinds.” For when we established it according to Rava, he needed to make a distinction: since “even all” also came [to apply to] the ritual impurity of creeping animals, perforce “even all” was to exclude them from [contracting impurity at a size of] three by three [fingerbreadths], like the law of leprosy, and “or a garment” was to include [them at a size of] three by three [handbreadths]. And even though other garments do not become ritually impure in leprosy — for they were excluded by two exclusions — they were included regarding creeping animals. However, according to Rav Pappa, we do not need to make a distinction: for since other garments were included regarding creeping animals, they were included for the entire rule of wool and linen — whether for three [by three fingerbreadths] or for three [by three handbreadths].

Rashi on Shabbat 27a:10:2.hebrew: בהדיא כתיבי ביה - צמר ופשתים — לא תלבש שעטנז וגו':
Rashi on Shabbat 27a:10:2.english: They are explicitly written in it - [Namely,] wool and linen — [as it is written:] “You shall not wear shaatnez...”

Rashi on Shabbat 27a:1:1.hebrew: מנא ליה - לרבי שמעון שום טומאה בשאר בגדים, הואיל ושאר בגדים הסתומים למדין הן מן המפורש:
Rashi on Shabbat 27a:1:1.english: From where does he [derive it] - [From where does] Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai [derive] any ritual impurity in other garments, since other, unspecified garments are learned from the specified [garment]?

Rashi on Shabbat 27a:1:2.hebrew: מאו בגד - דכתיב בשרצים, "או" ריבויא הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 27a:1:2.english: From “or a garment” - As it is written regarding creeping animals, [and the word] “or” is an inclusion.

Rashi on Shabbat 27a:1:3.hebrew: דתניא - ל"ג, דאי מתניתא היא, היכי פליג עלה אביי ואמר: מיבעיא ליה לשלש על שלש? הא תנא תני בהדיא: שלשה על שלשה בשאר בגדים מניין! אלא, דרשא דרבא היא:
Rashi on Shabbat 27a:1:3.english: “As it was taught” - We do not maintain this reading, for if it were a baraita, how could Abaye disagree with it and say: “He needs it for [a swatch of] three by three [fingerbreadths]”? Behold, the tanna explicitly teaches: “Three by three [handbreadths] in other garments, from where [is it derived]?” Rather, it is the exposition of Rava.

Rashi on Shabbat 27a:3:1.hebrew: גלי רחמנא בנגעים - דרבייה מן והבגד, וה"ה לשרצים — דכיון דכתיב בהן בגד כי התם, מיניה ילפינן בבנין אב:
Rashi on Shabbat 27a:3:1.english: The Torah revealed in the case of leprosy - That [the Torah] included it [a swatch of three by three fingerbreadths] from "And the garment" [Leviticus 13:47], and the same is true with regard to creeping animals — for since "garment" is written regarding them just as [it is written] there, we derive from it by a prototype [binyan av].

Rashi on Shabbat 27a:4:1.hebrew: שרצים אין שתי וערב מטמא בהן - דבגד כתיב בהו, ולא שתי ולא ערב:
Rashi on Shabbat 27a:4:1.english: [Regarding] creeping animals, warp and woof do not become ritually impure through them - For "a garment" is written concerning them, and neither warp nor woof.

Rashi on Shabbat 27a:5:1.hebrew: ואידך אי ס"ד - ורבא אמר לך: על כרחיך לשלשה על שלשה בשאר בגדים אתא, דאילו ג' על ג' בצמר ופשתים בשרצים מנגעים יליף. דאי נגעים חמירי, לכתוב רחמנא האי ריבויא בשרצים ולשתוק מריבויא דהבגד בנגעים; אלא לדרשא אחריתי אתא:
Rashi on Shabbat 27a:5:1.english: And the other: If it should enter your mind - And Rava [could] say to you: Perforce, [the verse] comes for [a swatch of] three by three [handbreadths] in other garments, for as for three by three [fingerbreadths] of wool and linen regarding creeping animals, he derives [it] from leprosy. For if leprosy were [indeed] more stringent, the Merciful One should have written this inclusion regarding creeping animals and remained silent regarding the inclusion of “the garment” in leprosy; rather, [the verse in creeping animals] came for another exposition.

Rashi on Shabbat 27a:6:1.english: In a lentil-bulk - And [for] leprosy, we require [the size of] a split bean.

Rashi on Shabbat 27a:7:1.hebrew: מפיק מאידך - כלומר, מוצא הוא מסברת אידך תנא דפליג עליה — דאשכחן דמרבי שאר בגדים לטומאת שרצים:
Rashi on Shabbat 27a:7:1.english: Diverges from the other - That is to say, he departs from the reasoning of the other Tanna, who disagrees with him — for we find that he includes other garments for the ritual impurity of creeping animals.

Rashi on Shabbat 27a:7:2.hebrew: של עזים - קרי נוצה, על שם שאין גוזזין אותם, אלא מורטין:
Rashi on Shabbat 27a:7:2.english: [That] of goats - [The Tanna] calls [it] down [notzah] because they do not shear them, but rather pluck [them].

Rashi on Shabbat 27a:8:1.hebrew: רבא אמר כי לית ליה - לתנא דרישא, בשאר בגדים בשרצים ג' על ג', דילמד סתום מן המפורש. אבל שלשה על שלשה בשרצים אית ליה בהו, דאיתרבו מאו בגד:
Rashi on Shabbat 27a:8:1.english: Rava said: When he does not hold - [This refers] to the Tanna of the first [baraita]: [when he does not hold that they become impure] in other garments regarding creeping animals, [it is only for a swatch of] three by three [fingerbreadths], for the unspecified [passage] should be learned from the explicit [one]. But [regarding a cloth of] three by three [handbreadths] in [the case of] creeping animals, he does hold [that impurity applies] to them, for they were included from [the verse], “Or a garment.”

Rashi on Shabbat 27a:9:1.hebrew: הדר ביה רבא מההיא - ואמר דתנא דבי רבי ישמעאל ורשב"א אמרו דבר אחד, ולאו כאביי, אלא דלתרוייהו: בשאר בגדים, טומאת ג' על ג' ליכא, שלשה על שלשה איכא:
Rashi on Shabbat 27a:9:1.english: Rava retracted that [opinion] - And [he now] says that the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said the same thing, and not in accordance with Abaye; rather, that according to both of them, in other garments there is no ritual impurity for [a swatch of] three by three [fingerbreadths], [but] there is [ritual impurity for a cloth of] three by three [handbreadths].

Rashi on Shabbat 27a:9:2.hebrew: ואיבעית אימא הא - שמעתא דסיפא לאו רבא אמרה, אלא רב פפא אמרה — לאוקמי תרוייהו תרי תנאי דרבי ישמעאל כהדדי, ולמימר דמודה תנא דרישא דיש טומאת שרצים בשאר בגדים:
Rashi on Shabbat 27a:9:2.english: And if you wish, say: This - The teaching of the latter clause was not said by Rava, but rather Rav Pappa said it, [in order] to establish both of the two tannaim of the school of Rabbi Yishmael in agreement with each other, and to say that the tanna of the first [baraita] concedes that there is ritual impurity of creeping animals in other garments.

Tosafot on Shabbat 27a:11:1.hebrew: אלא הא דרב פפא בדותא היא - תימה לר"י: דבריש יבמות (גם זה שם) משמע, דלתנא דבי רבי ישמעאל "אף כל" לאתויי כלאים, כי היכי דליהוי "צמר ופשתים" מופנה למדרש סמוכין להתיר כלאים בציצית. וי"ל: דהיינו עד דלא ידע ד"שעטנז" לאפנויי; אבל במסקנא, דאמר לרבנן "שעטנז" לאפנויי, הכי נמי לתנא דבי ר' ישמעאל, ו"צמר ופשתים" לגופייהו אתו — הלכך לא צריך "אף כל" לאתויי כלאים. וא"ת: לתנא דבי ר' ישמעאל, "צמר ופשתים" גבי לבישה מ"מ ל"ל? דמדכתיב: "ובגד כלאים שעטנז לא יעלה עליך", שמעינן דכל בגדים צמר ופשתים הן! וי"ל: דה"א דווקא העלאה, אבל בלבישה כל תרי מיני אסירי. והשתא, ליכא למימר לתנא דבי ר' ישמעאל דתיתי "שעטנז" "שעטנז" מהעלאה, כדאמר בריש סוגיא ביבמות (דף ד: ושם) — דהא השתא איצטריך "שעטנז" לאפנויי למדרש סמוכין, ולא מופנה למדרש מיניה גזירה שוה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 27a:11:1.english: “Rather, this [statement] of Rav Pappa is a mistake” - [This is] puzzling to the Ri, for at the beginning of Yevamot (this too is there [4b]) it implies that according to the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael, “even all” [comes] to include diverse kinds [kilayim], in order that “wool and linen” would be free [mufneh] to expound the juxtaposition [semukhin], to permit diverse kinds in ritual fringes [tzitzit]. And one can say that this was [said only] before [the Gemara] knew that “sha’atnez” is free [to be expounded]; but in the conclusion [Yevamot 5b], where it says according to the Rabbis that “sha’atnez” is free, so too according to the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael, and “wool and linen” come for their own sake [to teach that the prohibition of wearing diverse kinds applies only to wool and linen] — therefore, he does not need “even all” to include diverse kinds. And if you say: According to the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael, why do I need “wool and linen” regarding wearing in any case? For since it is written: “And a garment of diverse kinds, sha’atnez, shall not come upon you” (Leviticus 19:19), we learn [from his rule that unspecified garments are wool and linen] that all garments are wool and linen! And one can say that [without it] I would have said [that this limitation applies] specifically to placing [the garment upon oneself], but regarding wearing, any two kinds are forbidden. And now, one cannot say according to the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael that [wearing] should be derived [via a verbal analogy of] “sha’atnez” [and] “sha’atnez” from placing, as [the Gemara] said at the beginning of the sugya in Yevamot (4b, and there) — for behold, now “sha’atnez” was needed to be freed to expound the juxtaposition [to ritual fringes], and is not free to derive a verbal analogy [gezeirah shavah] from it.

Tosafot on Shabbat 27a:1:1.hebrew: נפקא ליה מאו בגד דתניא בגד כו' - פירש בקונטרס דלא גרסינן "דתניא", דאי ברייתא היא — היכי פליג אביי? ולאו פירכא היא: דהא אביי מודה דאו אתא לרבות שאר בגדים לאידך תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל, כדאמר אביי גופיה בסמוך, והיינו ההיא ברייתא גופיה דלקמן, אלא שקיצרה רבא. והא דקאמר לאביי: "האי 'או' מאי עביד ליה?" — היינו אליבא דרשב"א והיך תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל; אבל לאידך תנא דבי ר' ישמעאל, אתא או לרבות שאר בגדים, אפי' לשלש על שלש, כדפריש' לעיל. ולרבא, דאמר דאידך תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל לא מרבה שאר בגדים אלא לשלשה על שלשה, לא מפיק האי תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל מאידך. וה"נ דהוה מצי למיבעיא הכא: "ורבא, האי 'או' להך תנא דבי ר' ישמעאל מאי עביד ליה?" — דלא פליגי אביי ורבא אלא אליבא דרשב"א, וכמו שדורש אביי, כן צריך למדרש רבא אליבא תנא דבי ר' ישמעאל דהכא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 27a:1:1.english: He derives it from "or a garment," as it was taught: "Garment," etc. - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained that we do not maintain the reading "as it was taught [in a baraita]," for if it is a baraita, how could Abaye dispute [it]? But this is not a [valid] objection, for Abaye concedes that "or" comes to include other garments according to the other tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael, as Abaye himself states nearby; and that is that very baraita itself [cited] below, except that Rava abbreviated it. And that which [the Gemara] asks to Abaye: "This 'or,' what does he do with it?" — that is according to Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar and that [first] tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael; but according to the other tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael, "or" comes to include other garments even for three by three [fingerbreadths], as we explained earlier. And according to Rava, who says that the other tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael includes other garments only for three by three [handbreadths], he does not differentiate this tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael from the other. And here too, [the Gemara] could have asked here: "And Rava, this 'or,' according to that [first] tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael, what does he do with it?" — for Abaye and Rava disagree only according to Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar, and just as Abaye interprets [it], so too Rava must interpret according to the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael here.

Tosafot on Shabbat 27a:1:2.hebrew: תלמוד לומר או בגד - תימה, דלקמן בפרק במה אשה יוצאה (דף שג:) דרשינן מאו בגד דאריג כל שהוא טמא. וכי תימא: שקולים הם ויבואו שניהם — מ"מ, כי פריך: "ואביי, האי או בגד מאי עביד ליה?" — לימא דאיצטריך לאריג כל שהוא! ואפי' אם נמחק שם ספרים דכתוב בהן "או בגד", וניגרוס דיליף מאו בבגד פשתים דכתיב גבי נגעים — הניחא לרבא, דיליף שרצים מנגעים על ידי דגלי רחמנא, וה"ה לענין אריג כל שהוא; אלא לאביי, מאי איכא למימר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 27a:1:2.english: "The verse states: 'Or a garment'" - [This is] puzzling, for later in the chapter [entitled] Bameh Ishah Yotzei'ah (63b), we derive from "or a garment" that woven fabric of any size is ritually impure. And if you should say that they are equally balanced and both may be derived — nevertheless, when [the Gemara] challenges: "And Abaye, what does he do with this 'or a garment'?" — let [the Gemara] say that it was needed for woven fabric of any size! And even if we were to delete [the reading in] those books where it is written "or a garment," and emend the text [to read] that it is derived from "or in a linen garment," which is written regarding leprosy — this is well according to Rava, who derives [the laws of] creeping animals from leprosy since the Merciful One revealed [it], and the same applies regarding woven fabric of any size; but according to Abaye, what is there to say?

Tosafot on Shabbat 27a:4:1.hebrew: מה לנגעים שכן שתי וערב טמא בהן - אבל בשרצים לא, כדאמר בפרק במה אשה (לקמן שבת דף סד.): יכול שאני מרבה את החבלים ואת המשיחות? ת"ל שק — מה שק טווי ואריג, אף כל טווי ואריג:
Tosafot on Shabbat 27a:4:1.english: "What [comparison is there] to leprosy, as warp and woof are ritually impure through them" - But with regard to creeping animals, [they do] not [become ritually impure], as [the Gemara] states in the chapter [entitled] Bameh Ishah (below, Shabbat 64a): "I might [have thought] that I should include ropes and cords? The verse states: 'Sack' — just as a sack is spun and woven, so too, everything [must be] spun and woven."

Tosafot on Shabbat 27a:5:1.hebrew: אי ס"ד נגעים חמירי - הא ודאי דנגעים חמירי! אלא מפר' הר"ם, דה"ק: אי ס"ד כדקאמרת, דאו בגד לרבות ג' על ג' בצמר ופשתים — דהא נגעים חמירי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 27a:5:1.english: "If it should enter your mind that leprosy is more stringent" - Surely it is certain that leprosy is more stringent [than creeping animals]! Rather, Harav R. Meir explains that this is what [Rava] is saying: If it should enter your mind as you said, that "or a garment" [comes] to include [a cloth of] three by three [fingerbreadths] in wool and linen, because leprosy is indeed more stringent [and creeping animals could not be derived from it].

Tosafot on Shabbat 27a:6:1.hebrew: שכן מטמא בכעדשה - ורבא, אע"ג דפירכא גמורה היא, לא חשיב ליה; דלא הוי אלא גילוי מילתא בעלמא, דגלי רחמנא בנגעים דג' על ג' קרוי בגד בצמר ופשתים, והוא הדין בשרצים. והקשה ה"ר יעקב מקורביי"ל הקדוש: ונימא ק"ו [הבי]: מה שתי וערב, דטהור בשרצים, טמא בנגעים — ג'על ג', שטמא בשרצים, אינו דין שטמא בנגעים? ויש לומר: דכלים יוכיחו, שמטמא בשרצים ולא בנגעים; אף אני אביא ג' על ג'. וכי תימא: מה לכלים, שכן אין מטמאין ואין נעשין אהל המת במחובר? דג' על ג' נמי אין נעשה אהל, כיון דלית ביה פותח טפח. אי נמי: שק יוכיח. אי נמי: בגד צבוע ובגד נכרי יוכיח, שטמא בשרצים ולא בנגעים, כדאמר בת"כ. וא"ת: דהכא משמע דעדשה הוי פחות מכגריס; ותימה לר"י: בפסחים, בריש "אלו דברים" (פסחים ד' סז:), קאמר: "מצורע חמור מבעל קרי, שכן טעון פריעה ופרימה" — "אדרבה, בעל קרי חמור, שכן מטמא במשהו!" — "סבר ליה כרבי נתן, דאמר: כחתימת פי האמה"; משמע דחתימת פי האמה לא הוי פחות מכגריס. והתם, לעיל מיניה, קאמר: "זב חמור משרץ, שכן טומאה יוצאה עליו מגופו" — ואי כעדשה הוי פחות מגריס ומחתימת פי האמה, ליפרוך: מה לשרץ שכן מטמא בכעדשה?! ומיהו, אי לא משמעתיה, מסברא אין להקשות; דאיכא למימר: דכעדשה, שהיא עבה, כדמרדד לה הוי רחבה טפי מגריס:
Tosafot on Shabbat 27a:6:1.english: For they transmit impurity with a lentil-bulk - And [as for] Rava, even though it is a complete refutation, he does not take it into account, because it is merely a disclosure of the matter [gilui milta be'alma] — that the Merciful One revealed with regard to leprosy that [a cloth of] three by three [fingerbreadths] is called a "garment" in wool and linen, and the same applies to creeping animals. And the holy Rabbi Jacob of Corbeil raised a difficulty: But let us state an a fortiori argument [kal vachomer] [as follows]: Just as warp and woof, which are pure with regard to creeping animals, are impure with regard to leprosy, [a cloth of] three by three [fingerbreadths], which is impure with regard to creeping animals, is it not logical that it should be impure with regard to leprosy? And one can say that vessels can prove [otherwise], for they become impure with creeping animals and not with leprosy; so too, I will bring [a cloth of] three by three [fingerbreadths, that it does not become impure with leprosy]. And if you say: What [comparison is there] to vessels, as they do not become impure and do not become a corpse-tent when attached [to the ground]? [That is no refutation, because a cloth of] three by three [fingerbreadths] also does not become a tent, since it lacks an opening of a handbreadth [poté'ach téfach]. Alternatively, sackcloth can prove [otherwise]. Alternatively, a dyed garment and a gentile's garment can prove [otherwise], for they are impure with regard to creeping animals and not with regard to leprosy, as [the Sifra] states in Torat Kohanim. And if you say that here it implies that a lentil-bulk is smaller than a split-bean; and [this poses] a difficulty to the Ri: In Pesachim, at the beginning of [the chapter entitled] Elu Devarim (Pesachim 67b), [the Gemara] says: "A leper is more stringent than one who has had a seminal emission, for he is required to tear his garments and let his hair grow wild." [The Gemara objects:] "On the contrary, one who has had a seminal emission is more stringent, for he transmits impurity with any amount!" [The Gemara answers:] "He holds in accordance with Rabbi Natan, who said: Like the amount that seals the opening of the penis." This implies that the amount that seals the opening of the penis is not smaller than a split-bean. And there, earlier in that [discussion], [the Gemara] says: "A zav is more stringent than a creeping animal, for impurity issues upon him from his own body." And if a lentil-bulk is smaller than a split-bean and than the amount that seals the opening of the penis, let [the Gemara] challenge: What [comparison is there] to a creeping animal, for it transmits impurity with a lentil-bulk?! However, were it not for the implication [of our Gemara], based on logical reasoning [alone] one should not raise this difficulty; for one could say that a lentil-bulk, which is thick, when one flattens it out, becomes wider than a split-bean.

Tosafot on Shabbat 27a:7:1.hebrew: מניין לרבות צמר גמלים - וא"ת: צמר גמלים אמאי לא הוי בכלל צמר, ומה צריך ריבוי? וי"ל: דסתם צמר הוא של כבשים, אבל של גמלים לא איקרי צמר סתם אלא צמר גמלים, וכן שאר צמר; והואיל דיש להם שם לווי, איצטריך ריבוי — כדאמר באלו טרפות (חולין דף סב:): "אזוב", ולא אזוב כוחלית:
Tosafot on Shabbat 27a:7:1.english: "From where [is it derived] to include camels' wool" - And if you say: Why is camels' wool not included under "wool", and why is an amplification needed? One can say that unqualified "wool" is that of sheep, but that of camels is not called simply "wool", but rather "camels' wool", and so too other [types of] wool. And since they have an accompanying modifier, an amplification was needed — as [the Gemara] says in [the chapter entitled] Elu Tereifot (Chullin 62b): "Hyssop" — and not cochlite hyssop.

Tosafot on Shabbat 27a:7:2.hebrew: ונוצה של עזים - תימה: מאי איצטריך ריבוי לנוצה של עזים? הא כתיב שק בהדיא בקרא, ושק הוי מדבר הבא מן העזים, כדמוכח בפרק במה אשה (לקמן שבת דף סד:). ותירץ ר"י: דשק הוי מן השער של עזים, וההיא מיקרי שער ולא נוצה; ומן הדק, דאיקרי נוצה, עושים בגדים ולא שק, ועל שם שמורטין אותה כמו נוצת התרנגולין קרי ליה נוצה. ואור"י: דכן משמע בפרק ראשית הגז (חולין דף קלז.), דקאמר: דראשית הגז אינו נוהג אלא ברחלים, דאמר קרא: ראשית גז צאנך, ואתיא גיזה גיזה מגז כבשי יתחמם (איוב ל״א:כ׳). ופריך התם: ונילף גיזה גיזה מבכור, ויהא נוהג אף בשוורים? אמר קרא: תתן לו — ולא לשקו. ופריך: נוצה של עזים ליחייב? אלמא נוצה לא הויא בכלל שק:
Tosafot on Shabbat 27a:7:2.english: "And goats' down" - It is astonishing: Why was an inclusion necessary for goats' down? Isn't sackcloth explicitly written in the verse, and sackcloth is [made from] material that comes from goats, as is proven in the chapter "Bameh Ishah" (below, Shabbat 64b)? And the Ri answered that sackcloth is [made] from the hair of goats, and that is called "hair" and not "down"; whereas from the fine [hair], which is called "down," they make garments and not sackcloth. And because they pluck it like the down of chickens, it is called "down." And the Ri says that this is indeed indicated in the chapter "Reishit HaGez" (Chullin 137a), which states that [the mitzva of] the first of the shearing applies only to ewes, as the verse states: "The first of the shearing of your flock [you shall give him]" (Deuteronomy 18:4), and it is derived [via a verbal analogy of] "shearing" [and] "shearing" from "From the shearing of my sheep he was warmed" (Job 31:20). And [the Gemara] challenges there: But let us derive "shearing" [and] "shearing" from a firstborn, and let it apply to oxen as well? The verse states: "[You shall] give to him" — and not for his sack. And [the Gemara] challenges: [If so,] let goats' down be obligated? Consequently, down is not included under sackcloth.

Tosafot on Shabbat 27a:9:1.hebrew: הדר ביה רבא מההיא - ומשום שלא יחלוק ההוא תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל אהך, הדר ביה מההיא דלעיל ולא מהך דהכא. ואית ליה לרבא: "אף כל" — לאתויי שרצים. וא"ת: בריש יבמות (דף ד: ושם), היכי פריך הש"ס: "והא תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל לית ליה דרבא"? ההיא ד"הכנף מין כנף" — מנא ליה דלית ליה? הא רבא אית ליה ד"אף כל" קאי אשרצים! דאי לאו "אף כל", ה"א דמיירי גבי שרצים בכל בגדים, ו"או" — לג' על ג'; אבל השתא דאמר "אף כל" צמר ופשתים, איצטריך "או" לרבות שלשה על שלשה בשאר בגדים, אבל שלש על שלש בשאר בגדים — לא. וי"ל: דהתם קאמר אליבא דרב נחמן בר יצחק, דאמר: "אף כל" — לאתויי ציצית; דהשתא ודאי לית ליה דרבא, דאיהו מחייב שאר מינים בציצית:
Tosafot on Shabbat 27a:9:1.english: Rava retracted that [opinion] - And in order that that tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael should not disagree with this one, he retracted that [statement] from above, and not this [statement] from here. And Rava maintains [that the derivation of] "even all" [comes] to include creeping animals. And if you will say: At the beginning of Yevamot (4b, and there), how does the Gemara challenge, "And does not the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael disagree with Rava?" That [derivation] of "the corner" [meaning fringes from] the same kind as the corner — from where does [the Gemara] know that he does not accept it? Behold, Rava maintains that "even all" applies to creeping animals! For if not for "even all," I would have said that regarding creeping animals [the verse] is dealing with all garments, and "or" [comes to include a cloth of] three by three; but now that [the tanna] said "even all" [garments must be] wool and linen, "or" was needed to include [a cloth of] three by three [handbreadths] in other garments, while three by three [fingerbreadths] in other garments [is] not [ritually impure]. And one can say: There [in Yevamot], [the Gemara] speaks according to Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak, who said that "even all" [comes] to include ritual fringes; for now [under that view], [the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael] certainly does not accept Rava's [opinion], as he [Rava] obligates other materials in ritual fringes.

Tosafot on Shabbat 27a:9:2.hebrew: רב פפא אמרה - לא בעי למימר "רב נחמן בר יצחק אמרה", דאמר "אף כל לאתויי ציצית" — דאין לטעות ולהחליף דברי רבא לרב נחמן, אלא ברב פפא, שהיה תלמידו ומלך אחריו; וכשהיה אומר דבר, לא היו יודעים אם מדעתו אמרה או למדה לפני רבו:
Tosafot on Shabbat 27a:9:2.english: "Rav Pappa said this" - [The Gemara] did not want to say: "Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said this" — who stated: "Even all [garments] comes to include tzitzit" — for one would not err and confuse the words of Rava with [those of] Rav Naḥman, but rather [only] with Rav Pappa, who was his disciple and succeeded him in leadership; and when he would state a teaching, they did not know whether he said it from his own reasoning or had learned it before his teacher.
